scenes.headline: How pmndrs math and TypeGPU share one vector
scenes.sub: Out-parameters on the CPU, value types on the GPU
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Umber! Two TypeScript libraries, two answers to one question: who owns a vector?

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: math keeps every vector a plain array the caller owns and writes into it; TypeGPU turns typed TypeScript into WGSL. They meet at the buffer.
scenes.say: Math keeps each vector a plain array you own and writes into it. TypeGPU compiles typed TypeScript into shaders. They meet at the buffer.

left.title: Every op allocates
left.say: Usually each vector op returns a fresh array. My two-bone solver, written that way, makes nine per solve.

right.title: Out-parameters
right.say: Math passes the output first and writes into it. Nothing is allocated per call.

scenes.title: From an IK solve to a shader

steps.say: A hand needs to reach a target. Math solves the limb on the CPU, into arrays allocated once.
The results are plain arrays. A matrix is sixteen numbers, column by column, as the GPU expects.
TypeGPU's buffer write takes those arrays as they are; the schema knows the padding.
A TypeScript shader marked use gpu reads the buffer. TypeGPU compiles it to WGSL.

scenes.title: The elbow, with square roots only
scenes.say: A two-bone limb has a closed form: the elbow sits where two circles meet.

parts.note: how far along the line to the target
parts.say: A is how far along the line to the target.

parts.note: how far off it; the sign picks the bend
parts.say: H is how far off it, and its sign picks the bend. No trig.

scenes.label: cold-start targets FABRIK left more than 0.01 away
scenes.say: Math ships FABRIK, an iterative solver. From a cold start, my run left two hundred seventy-two of thirteen hundred sixty-eight targets short, mostly near the shoulder.

scenes.quote: the playful web's most optimized math engine
scenes.say: The launch called it the most optimized. Its hundred and twenty-three benchmarks only compare it with its own earlier runs.

scenes.text: Out-parameters where a garbage collector lives, value types where it does not. The buffer is where they meet.
scenes.mark: The buffer is where they meet.

recap: math: plain arrays you own, written in place
TypeGPU: typed buffers, shaders written in TypeScript
Two bones need square roots, not iterations
scenes.say: To recap: math writes into arrays you own, TypeGPU types the buffer and the shader, and two bones need only square roots.
